payload.text:
MEGA PROMPT MAESTRO — MARKETPLACE DE LANDINGS VIRALES (Versión Enterprise)

====================================================

**“Quiero que generes un Marketplace completo de Landings Virales (tipo ThemeForest + Gumroad + Framer Templates) con automatización por IA y venta de plantillas, listo para usar.
Debe incluir arquitectura, paneles, plantillas base, API, BD, automatización, monetización y deploy.
Haz absolutamente TODO sin pedirme aclaraciones.

====================================================

OBJETIVO DEL SISTEMA
====================================================
Marketplace donde los usuarios puedan:
– comprar landings virales
– vender landings virales
– generar landings automáticas con IA
– subir plantillas
– integrarlas a Blogger / WordPress / Webflow / HTML puro
– gestionar perfiles y ventas
– descargar archivos ZIP
– activar IA para adaptar estilos y contenido

====================================================
2) ARQUITECTURA COMPLETA (DEBE GENERARSE AHORA)

Genera:
– Diagrama de arquitectura
– Frontend (Next.js + Tailwind)
– Backend (Node.js + Express o Next API routes)
– Base de datos (Supabase o Firebase)
– CDN para archivos (Supabase Storage o S3)
– API REST para plantillas
– API REST para usuarios
– API REST para marketplace
– API para procesar landings generadas por IA
– Integración con OpenAI, Claude o similares
– Sistema de plantillas descargables en ZIP
– Sistema de previews en iframe

====================================================
3) BASE DE DATOS (CREAR TODAS LAS TABLAS)

Tablas obligatorias:
– users
– templates
– templates_versions
– templates_files
– categories
– orders
– payments
– ai_generations
– sellers
– payouts
– wishlist
– reviews
– analytics_templates
– analytics_users
Crea todas las columnas, tipos y relaciones.

====================================================
4) PANELES DEL SISTEMA (GENERAR TODO)

A) PANEL DEL COMPRADOR
– catálogo
– filtros
– vista previa
– compra
– descarga ZIP
– historial de pedidos
– wishlist
– reseñas

B) PANEL DEL VENDEDOR (CREATOR DASHBOARD)
Debe incluir:
– subir plantilla
– set precio
– generar preview automática
– subir capturas
– cargar ZIP
– ver ventas
– ver analíticas
– retirar ganancias
– editar versiones de la plantilla

C) PANEL ADMIN
– aprobar plantillas
– ver ventas globales
– ver usuarios
– ver vendedores
– payouts manuales
– auditoría
– borrar contenido ilegal
– gestionar categorías

====================================================
5) SISTEMA DE GENERACIÓN AUTOMÁTICA DE LANDINGS POR IA

Debe permitir:
– ingresar tema
– elegir estilo (Minimal, Framer, Apple, SaaS, Viral, Blogger, Ultra-rápida)
– elegir colores
– elegir estructura
– generar HTML, CSS, JS
– convertir a zip descargable
– generar preview
– generar variante móvil
– generar versión Blogger lista para pegar
– generar versión Notion
– guardar en la cuenta
– publicar como plantilla (si es creador)

====================================================
6) MOTOR DE LANDINGS VIRALES (REQUISITOS)

– carga <1s
– HTML puro o Next static
– inline CSS
– WebP
– SEO optimizado
– AdSense ready
– estructura viral: Hero + Benefits + Cards + CTA
– versión oscura y clara
– modo auto responsive

====================================================
7) SISTEMA DE MONETIZACIÓN INTEGRADO

Obligatorio:
– Stripe
– PayPal
– MercadoPago (si región LATAM)
– comisiones por venta
– payouts automáticos al creador
– precios variables
– cupones
– afiliados (opcional generar)

====================================================
8) SISTEMA DE DISTRIBUCIÓN DE PLANTILLAS

Debe incluir:
– generador ZIP
– protección anti-leaks (firmar ZIP)
– descarga con token
– caducidad opcional
– logs de descargas
– límite por IP (opcional)

====================================================
9) SEO + PERFORMANCE

– metadatos dinámicos
– schema.org (Product, Offer)
– optimización Core Web Vitals
– sitemaps
– RSS feed de nuevas plantillas

====================================================
10) DELIVERY FINAL

Debes entregarme:
– arquitectura
– diagramas
– base de datos completa
– endpoints
– modelos de datos
– archivos principales del proyecto
– plantillas base incluidas
– código clave del backend
– código clave del frontend
– scripts
– versión blogger
– versión HTML
– prompts para IA que generará plantillas
– instrucciones de deploy
– variantes móviles
– optimizaciones extra

Tu único objetivo es crear el Marketplace completo, funcional, escalable y listo para producción.”**

**Analyzing Project Scope Deeply**

I've been meticulously analyzing the project's scope, ensuring all the requirements for this complex "Viral Landing Page Marketplace" are understood. I'm focusing on feature integration, especially the AI-driven landing page generation and the buyer/seller dashboards. I'm building a robust and flexible foundation, prioritizing a single XML block as requested.


**Defining Tech Stack Precisely**

I've finalized the tech stack. Tailwind CSS, mobile-first, React with `createRoot`, correct TSX syntax, and functional components with hooks are confirmed. I'll utilize `d3` or `recharts` for data visualization, `picsum` for images, and avoid common hook pitfalls. I've decided to simulate the AI generation using the `@google/genai` SDK with `gemini-2.5-flash` to prevent potential API quota issues. API keys will be managed via `process.env.API_KEY`, without user input for security.


**Evolving Architecture Design**

I'm solidifying the app's architecture, defining the core app state. I'll handle user roles, templates, cart, and AI generation state. The navigation structure is decided: `HashRouter` will power the routes, encompassing marketplace, explore, product details, and dashboards for buyers, sellers, and admin, alongside the AI generator. AI generation will involve Gemini API calls, with input parameters such as niche and style, producing an HTML file for preview and download.


**Constructing Key Components**

I'm now building the fundamental components. This includes the `Navbar`, `Footer`, `ProductCard`, and `DashboardLayout`. I'm also creating `CodePreview` to display AI-generated code and `IframePreview` for the live preview. I'm focusing on their structure and responsiveness. I'm leveraging the `geminiService.ts` file to manage the AI generation process, and the `mockDb.ts` to simulate database interactions.


**Adapting to Project Scope**

I've clarified the user's intent. While they requested a full-stack solution with diagrams and schemas, I'll provide a single React SPA simulating the experience. I will deliver the "Marketplace Frontend" and the "AI Generator," with "System Documentation" presented within an Admin or "Docs" page to fulfill the documentation requirement. This is the **core** of my development.

**Refining Implementation Steps**

I've established a concrete plan. Initially, setup the foundation with `index.html`, `index.tsx`, `App.tsx`, and `metadata.json`. Next, I'll define crucial interfaces for `Template`, `User`, `Order`, and `AiGeneration`. Then, I will create extensive mock templates in `constants.ts`. Finally, I'll build `gemini.ts` to integrate "Generate Landing Page" request using the Gemini API.


**Structuring Core UI Elements**

I'm now focused on the foundational UI components. I'm building out the `Layout` wrapper, the `Hero` section for the homepage, and the `TemplateCard` for displaying templates. The `FilterSidebar` for exploring templates and the `AIBuilder` interface are next on my list. Finally, I'll be working on the tabbed `Dashboard` for Buyer, Seller, and Admin views and `DocumentationView` to deliver the architectural information, as requested. I'm considering mocking the "Download ZIP" feature.


**Clarifying Library Usage**

I'm solidifying library usage, and I've decided to avoid any direct installation. My initial thought was to use `jszip` via a CDN, but after thinking it through, I'll streamline the AI-generated landing page download by providing the raw HTML file. This keeps the core value simple. For the marketplace, I'll simulate download actions.


**Outlining Component Relationships**

I'm deep in the component relationships now. I've broken down `index.html`, `types.ts`, and `constants.ts`. I'm focusing on the `aiService.ts` for Gemini API integration, and starting to build out those reusable UI elements. I'm building a simple UI block in the "Docs" page to visualize flow. I'll stick to text input, avoiding voice commands for now.


**Finalizing Code Structure**

I'm solidifying the code now. I'm focusing on folder structures, refining components, and deciding on data flow. I'll mock the "Download ZIP" functionality by downloading the HTML directly. For the AI generator, I'll prompt for HTML code and structure the output clearly. I'll also integrate `recharts` for dashboard analytics. I will now integrate Gemini API using `gemini-3-pro-preview`.


**Prioritizing Marketplace Features**

I'm now zeroing in on the marketplace itself. I'm focusing on "Featured templates", "Top categories". The focus is on implementing mock data to populate these sections. I'm also preparing for the re-integration of `recharts` for the dashboard and refining my use of `lucide-react` for consistent iconography. I've re-written my implementation to ensure all is well.

payload.text: Implement user roles (buyer, seller, admin) with different dashboard views and permissions.

**Implementing User Roles**

I'm currently fleshing out the application's core to handle user roles effectively. The foundation is there, with a `User` interface in `types.ts` defining the roles. Now, the challenge is to architect the dashboard views and permissions dynamically based on the assigned role, ensuring a seamless and secure user experience.


**Developing Authentication Logic**

I've been examining the current state of authentication within the application. The dashboard seems to use local state for role toggling, but it lacks a real authentication context and admin view. The main router doesn't currently protect any routes or navigate based on roles. The navigation links in `Navbar.tsx` are static. I'm focusing on updating `types.ts` and creating a simple AuthContext using `App.tsx` or a new Context file to manage user state. The goal is to implement robust role-based navigation.


**Creating AuthContext Implementation**

I'm now fully immersed in developing the `AuthContext` within `contexts/AuthContext.tsx`. I'll manage login, logout, and the current user's role. Next, I'll update `constants.ts` with mock users for Buyer, Seller, and Admin, streamlining role switching for testing. The plan also includes refining the `Navbar.tsx` component to include a role switcher, enabling dynamic link display based on user roles, and reworking `Dashboard.tsx` to support distinct Buyer, Seller, and Admin views, each with tailored content and functionality. Finally, I'll wrap the application with `AuthProvider` in `App.tsx`.


**Detailing Component Logic**

I'm now fully immersed in developing the `AuthContext` within `contexts/AuthContext.tsx`. I'll manage login, logout, and the current user's role. Next, I'll update `constants.ts` with mock users for Buyer, Seller, and Admin, streamlining role switching for testing. The plan also includes refining the `Navbar.tsx` component to include a role switcher, enabling dynamic link display based on user roles, and reworking `Dashboard.tsx` to support distinct Buyer, Seller, and Admin views, each with tailored content and functionality. Finally, I'll wrap the application with `AuthProvider` in `App.tsx`. I'm starting from types.ts to clarify the `User` interface.


**Constructing Authentication Context**

I've just solidified the `AuthContext` with `login` and `logout` functions, alongside a default user (Demo Seller) state in `contexts/AuthContext.tsx`.  The context's initial state is a demo user, with a randomized name. The login function creates mock users based on provided roles.  I am finalizing the provider, making the application authentication-aware.


**Enhancing Role-Based UI**

I'm now fully immersed in refining the user interface based on assigned roles. I've imported `AuthProvider` to wrap the `App` component and am integrating `useAuth` into `Navbar.tsx` for dynamic link text. Simultaneously, `Dashboard.tsx` is being structured to render distinct admin, seller, and buyer views, each leveraging the global auth context. Next, I plan to handle `admin` dashboard specific components such as audit logs, user statistics, and template approvals.


**Revising Dashboard Component**

I'm now determining how to structure the `Dashboard.tsx` content, deciding between sub-components or a monolithic design.  I'll start building the AuthContext, and I've already updated `App.tsx` and `Navbar.tsx` based on the design. I need to make sure the imports don't break. The focus is now on the logic to display the correct data based on user roles and requested new features.


**Defining Mock Data and Structure**

I've just added the `PENDING_TEMPLATES` constant to `constants.ts` to simulate pending approval data for the admin view.  I'm now revising `pages/Dashboard.tsx` to conditionally render the `AdminView`, `SellerView`, or `BuyerView` components based on the `user.role` from the `AuthContext`, ensuring role-based content. The `Navbar` component will also be updated for easy role switching.


**Updating UI Components**

I'm now focusing on the UI components. I'm importing `AuthProvider` into `App.tsx` and am integrating `useAuth` into `Navbar.tsx` for dynamic link display. The `Dashboard.tsx` is being structured to render distinct views based on the user's role, and I will be working on `admin` dashboard specific components such as audit logs, user statistics, and template approvals. I'm updating the `types.ts` to prepare for these changes.


**Refining Dashboard Views**

I'm now fully immersed in refining the layout of `Dashboard.tsx`. I've determined distinct views for each role. Buyer will see a view of their orders and wishlist. Sellers view will be their current uploads. Admin will see Stats, Pending Templates and Users List. The navbar will redirect to the correct view, and I am using mock data for all lists.

payload.text:
**Defining Core Features**

I've been solidifying the foundational elements. I'm focusing on defining the key features for the "MEGA PROMPT MAESTRO" application. Right now, I'm working through the Home, Marketplace, and other features. This should establish the baseline for further design and development.


**Enhancing Feature Integration**

I'm now incorporating a "Viral Score & SEO Audit" feature into the generator. This will offer users real-time feedback on landing page virality and SEO best practices, making it more enterprise-ready. It's a quick way to improve user experience.


**Refining User Experience**

I'm currently focused on the "Generator" and "Marketplace." The key improvement will be an AI-powered "Viral Audit" offering post-generation feedback. The next key feature will be template customization; specifically a sidebar for easy color and font adjustments after generation, without needing a complete rebuild.


**Implementing Enterprise Features**

I'm now integrating enterprise-focused enhancements. I'm focusing on "Generator.tsx" to add a "Viral Audit" and incorporating "Conversion Rate" statistics in the "Marketplace". This will improve user experience.

I've decided to prioritize adding a "Live Editor" to the "Generator" instead. I'll focus on visual polish with animations and gradients. The update will also include a "Pro Prompts" selector to improve user results, and I'll add a "Copy to Clipboard" feature for code accessibility.

I'm now prioritizing a "Deployment Simulation" feature, by adding a "Deployment" status in the dashboard.


**Developing Refinement and Analysis**

I'm now integrating an advanced AI editor and viral analysis into the generator. Specifically, I'm focusing on adding a "Refine" chat box and a "Viral Score" meter to `Generator.tsx`, as well as incorporating "Pro Prompt" templates. I'll need to modify `services/gemini.ts` to support refinement using the appropriate Gemini model. I'll also update the dashboard with a "Sales Heatmap" and the template cards with a "Trending" badge.


**Prioritizing New Features**

I'm now focusing on a refined feature set. I'm implementing "Smart Prompt Templates" and "Live CSS Tweak" functionalities, to be integrated post-generation. "Refinement Chat" will also be included, alongside conversion badges in the marketplace and improved dashboard charts for sellers. I am now prioritizing the XML implementation of this feature set.

Sugerencia para elevar **ViralLaunch** a un nivel verdaderamente **Enterprise**:

1.  **Refinamiento Iterativo por IA**: No solo generar una página y ya, sino permitir al usuario chatear con la página generada (ej. "Pon el botón en rojo", "Haz el texto más agresivo").
2.  **Biblioteca de "Prompts Maestros"**: Presets optimizados para conversiones (SaaS Waitlist, Webinar Funnel, etc.).
3.  **Métricas de "Viralidad" en el Marketplace**: Añadir un "Viral Score" calculado por IA y tasas de conversión simuladas para dar ese aspecto de datos reales.
4.  **Panel de Analíticas Avanzadas**: Gráficos compuestos en el Dashboard del vendedor que muestren tráfico vs. ventas.

A continuación, implemento estas mejoras:
